name: Reasoning Models Know When They're Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification
authors: Anqi Zhang, Yulin Chen, Jane Pan, Chen Zhao, Aurojit Panda, Jinyang Li, He He; lead affiliation New York University (with NYU Shanghai)
venue: COLM 2025 (Conference on Language Modeling); originally arXiv preprint 2504.05419 (April 2025)
reflection_type: calibration/probing — a trained linear/MLP probe over the reasoning model's hidden states classifies the correctness of intermediate answers and is used as a learned verifier (self-verification via internal representations, not verbal self-critique)
feedback_source: hidden-state-probe: a binary classifier reads the model's last-layer hidden states at intermediate-answer positions. Probe supervision (training labels) comes from Gemini 2.0 Flash extracting/judging intermediate answers against ground-truth answers (ground-truth-oracle used only to label probe training data, not at inference)
iteration_structure: single-shot probing of a fixed reasoning trace; at inference the probe drives a confidence-thresholded early-exit that sequentially scores each intermediate answer chunk and truncates the chain-of-thought once confidence exceeds the threshold (no re-sampling or retry)
reflection_object: reasoning chain — specifically the intermediate answers within a long Chain-of-Thought (CoT). The probe reflects on the correctness of each intermediate answer encoded in the model's hidden states; the actionable use modifies the reasoning trace length (early exit). The probe itself is a separately trained artifact (gradient weight update on the small classifier, not the base model).
learning_locus: gradient_weight_update — a lightweight MLP/linear probe is trained (Adam, weighted BCE, grid search) on hidden-state representations; the base reasoning model's weights are frozen. The learned-signal lives in the trained probe rather than in-context.
requires_training: SFT-style supervised training of the probe only: a two-layer MLP (often degenerating to a linear probe, hidden size d=0) trained with weighted binary cross-entropy via Adam. No RL; the base reasoning model is not updated.
reward_or_critic_model: trained reward/critic model — the probe is a trained correctness classifier (verifier) over hidden states; it functions as a separate learned verifier of intermediate-answer correctness rather than self-as-judge or a verbal critic
distillation_target: model-weights (of the auxiliary probe): correctness information latent in the reasoning model's hidden states is distilled into a small trained classifier (probe) that is reused at inference as a verifier; no episodic-memory, skill library, or prompt artifact is produced
emergent_vs_engineered: Hybrid framing: the self-verification SIGNAL is RL/long-CoT-emergent — correctness information is found to be inherently (often linearly) encoded in reasoning models' hidden states and is far weaker in non-reasoning instruct models, suggesting it is acquired during long-CoT training. EXPLOITING it (the probe + early-exit) is engineered. Key finding: models encode correctness yet fail to exploit it during inference.
memory_type: none — no episodic memory, scratchpad reuse, or skill library; the only persistent learned artifact is the trained probe (a verifier), and analysis is over fixed reasoning traces
memory_persistence: n/a — the probe is trained once per (model, dataset) and applied at inference; there is no cross-episode experience accumulation. (Probe generalizes across some datasets, e.g. GSM8K<->MATH transfer, but this is OOD generalization, not memory.)
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a — no memory store to curate. Probe training data is down-sampled to <=1000 examples per dataset (pilot showed no performance loss); class imbalance is handled with a weighted BCE loss rather than memory curation.
error_localization_granularity: step-level / intermediate-answer-level — the probe scores correctness at each intermediate-answer chunk within the long CoT (a chunk being one reasoning path delimited by 'wait'/'double-check'/'alternatively' keywords). It also predicts future-answer correctness from earlier paragraph positions mid-chunk (look-ahead), i.e. before the intermediate answer is fully generated.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task — operates within a single problem's reasoning trace (verifying intermediate answers and deciding when to stop reasoning on that same problem). Cross-dataset probe transfer is studied as OOD generalization but the corrective mechanism is intra-task, not experience transfer across tasks.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: neither recovery nor avoidance in the trajectory-correction sense — the probe does not correct or re-route reasoning; it performs confidence-based early termination (exit when a correct intermediate answer is detected with high confidence), i.e. an efficiency/overthinking-mitigation intervention rather than mid-trajectory error correction or next-episode avoidance
task_domains: math reasoning and logical (QA/reasoning) tasks — verifiable-answer domains used to enable automatic correctness labeling
benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH, AIME (mathematical reasoning), and KnowLogic (a 5.4k multiple-choice knowledge-driven logical-reasoning benchmark). Reasoning models probed: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B/70B, R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B/7B/32B, and QwQ-32B; non-reasoning baseline Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
headline_result: A simple probe over hidden states verifies intermediate-answer correctness with ROC-AUC >0.7 (>0.9 for R1-Distill-Qwen-32B on AIME) and ECE <0.1 (well-calibrated). Used as a verifier for confidence-based early-exit on R1-Distill-Llama-8B / MATH: ~24% reduction in inference tokens at threshold 0.85 with maintained accuracy (88.2% vs no-exit), and 19% token reduction at threshold 0.9 with identical accuracy (88.6%).
baselines: (1) No early-exit (full reasoning) baseline accuracy on R1-Distill-Llama-8B/MATH; (2) static early-exit (terminate after a fixed number m of intermediate-answer chunks) as the comparison early-exit strategy; (3) probes trained on non-reasoning Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct representations (to show correctness encoding is much weaker without long-CoT training); plus ECE/Brier/ROC-AUC reported per model and dataset.
gains_vs_baseline: vs no-early-exit: ~24% fewer tokens at ~equal accuracy (88.2% vs full reasoning at threshold 0.85), 19% fewer tokens at identical 88.6% accuracy at threshold 0.9. vs static early-exit at equal token budget: up to +5% accuracy (confidence-based 87.4% at Thr=0.8 vs static ~82.5%); at matched accuracy (>85%) the confidence-based exit uses significantly fewer tokens than static (m=6). Probe on reasoning models markedly outperforms probe on non-reasoning Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (lower classification + higher calibration error for the latter).
compute_cost_profile: Reduces inference compute relative to full reasoning: ~19-24% fewer generated tokens via early-exit (max generation cap 10K tokens). The probe is extremely cheap to train (two-layer MLP, often a linear probe, batch size 64, <=200 epochs with early stopping, training sets down-sampled to <=1000 examples) and cheap to run (single forward read of last-layer hidden states per chunk). Labeling step uses Gemini 2.0 Flash to extract/judge intermediate answers during probing-data construction.
known_limitations: Probe does not stably generalize out-of-domain (e.g. logical-reasoning KnowLogic <-> math probes transfer poorly), and calibration degrades on harder OOD data such as AIME. Correctness encoding is weak in non-reasoning models, and the precise training origin of the self-verification ability remains unclear. The early-exit study is demonstrated on a single model/dataset (R1-Distill-Llama-8B on MATH). Probe training labels depend on a Gemini-based judge plus ground-truth answers (requires verifiable-answer tasks). Core caveat: models encode correctness but do not exploit it natively, so overthinking persists without the external probe-based intervention.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: At inference: self-verify via the model's own hidden states (no ground-truth label needed once the probe is trained). For probe TRAINING: oracle-label/ground-truth dependency — Gemini 2.0 Flash extracts intermediate answers and judges them against ground-truth answers to create the supervised probe labels. So the verifier is learned from oracle labels but applied label-free at test time.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive (efficiency, not accuracy uplift): early-exit maintains accuracy while cutting tokens, and beats static exit at matched budgets. It does not raise final accuracy beyond the model's full-reasoning ceiling; its value is mitigating overthinking. The probe's verification is reliable in-distribution but task-dependent OOD.
calibration_effect: improves / strongly positive on the calibration axis — trained probes are highly calibrated (ECE <0.1, e.g. as low as 0.01-0.03 in-distribution; Brier scores reported). Calibration can degrade on harder OOD data (e.g. AIME ECE up to ~0.25-0.31 for transferred probes). The central message is that reasoning models internally hold well-calibrated correctness signals they fail to use.
failure_attribution_capability: attributes-failing-step (in a soft sense) — the probe localizes correctness to specific intermediate-answer chunks/steps in the CoT and can flag a correct answer early; it is a correctness classifier rather than a multi-agent failure-attribution or counterfactual-localization method
failure_mode_addressed: overthinking — the paper directly targets and empirically demonstrates the overthinking failure mode of reasoning models (continuing to generate reasoning/re-checks even after a correct, high-confidence intermediate answer). Relates to underthinking/overthinking discussions and to superficial self-verification (models encode correctness but do not act on it).
builds_on: Internal-representation correctness probing (Azaria & Mitchell 2023; Burns et al. 2024 CCS-style linear probes), white-box uncertainty estimation outperforming black-box verbalized confidence (Xiong et al. 2024; Kapoor et al. 2024), learned verifiers / process reward models (Cobbe et al. 2021; Lightman et al. 2023), and overthinking/efficient-reasoning analyses of reasoning models (Chen et al. 2025; Sui et al. 2025); reasoning models DeepSeek-R1 (DeepSeek-AI et al. 2025), OpenAI o1, and QwQ-32B.
extended_by_or_inspired: Has been cited (~136 citations) by follow-up work on hidden-state-based confidence/early-exit and efficient reasoning for o1/R1-style models, including dynamic early-exit-in-reasoning methods (e.g. DEER, arXiv 2504.15895) and probing-based confidence/overthinking-mitigation studies. (Specific successor list beyond these is [uncertain].)
citation_count: 136 (Semantic Scholar, as of mid-2026); reference count 42
reasoning_model_native: Yes — the method specifically targets o1/R1-era long-CoT reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill series, QwQ-32B). The probed self-verification signal is shown to be a property of reasoning models, substantially weaker in the non-reasoning Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct counterpart, indicating it emerges from long-CoT training.
on_policy_distillation_link: Indirect — correctness information that is implicitly present in the reasoning model's on-policy long-CoT hidden states is distilled into an explicit lightweight probe/verifier. Not on-policy distillation in the policy-update sense (base model frozen), but it can be seen as distilling a latent self-verification skill into a reusable verifier that could inform training-time concision/overthinking objectives.
sample_efficiency: Very high for the probe: training sets down-sampled to <=1000 examples per (model, dataset) with no observed performance loss; probe often reduces to a linear probe (hidden size d=0). Trained <=200 epochs with early stopping, batch size 64, 8:2 train/val split. At inference the early-exit yields its token savings (~19-24%) without additional sampling.
